_comment: Species definitions. Base stats and presentation only; a live creature's current HP and energy belong to a pal_instance, never here (TECHNICAL_START.md, Pal Data vs Pal Instance). M11 replaces `model` and the colours with real rigged creatures without touching combat code.
_placeholder: M2 ships coloured capsules on purpose. CLAUDE.md forbids judging creature appeal on placeholders, so these are shaped for READABILITY at combat distance — clearly different silhouettes and clearly different colours — and nothing else.
_comment_catch: `catch_rate` is the species' base share of the catch formula in scripts/combat/catch_math.gd. Lower is rarer. Every species must declare one; tests/test_catch_math.gd fails the build if any is missing, because a creature that is accidentally trivial to catch is the kind of bug nobody reports.
_comment_names: Ids and display names for the wild roster are canon from `docs/art/wild/` — the owner's Meadows Wild Canon Pack, which supersedes `docs/art/ROSTER_MANIFEST.md` for these creatures (`docs/decisions/D13`). The meshes under them do not all match yet: Tuskroot is still a songbird from the Plumberry pack (`docs/decisions/D10`) and is the last stand-in in the table. Bramblebun WAS a duck and is not any more — it was produced properly from its own sheet.
_comment_scale: Creatures stand as PEERS to the 1.8m trainer, not as pets at his ankles. The owner set this after seeing the first three starters in the meadow: 'make the pals canonically about the same size as the character... I want them to have more emphasis and focus in the game'. Starters 1.55-1.70m, wild pals 1.35-2.00m so GAME_DESIGN.md 26's 'pal size should vary substantially' still holds around the new centre. The reference sheets' real-world sizes (Terrapup 0.45m at the shoulder) are the CREATURE'S biology, not its game scale, and the two are allowed to differ -- see docs/decisions/D12.
_comment_wild_stats: TUNABLE, all of them. The wild roster's statlines are set from the sheets' own ROLE and STRENGTHS lines and from nothing else: a digger is tougher than a scout, a tracker hits harder than it takes, a shell is defence and a raptor is not. Nobody has played a fight with any of them yet, so treat every number below as a first guess that combat feedback is expected to move.
_comment_wild_heights: Heights follow D13: D12's peer band, with the sheets' RELATIVE ordering preserved. The pack's own centimetre figures (Pipwing 0.25m body length, Galecrest 1.80m) are the creature's biology, not its game scale, exactly as sheets 01-04's figures already are. Pipwing and Bramblebun stay the smallest; Meadowhart, Galecrest and Tuskroot stay the largest.
_comment_evolution_size: An evolution is ALWAYS larger than the form it came from — the owner's rule, `docs/decisions/D17`. Every `evolves_into` target must have a strictly greater `placeholder.height` than its source. This constrains RELATIVE size inside a line only; it does not reopen D12/D13's settled 1.20-2.60m peer band. Mudsnout 1.40m -> Tuskroot 2.00m satisfies it, and satisfied it by accident until tests/test_evolution_links.gd started failing loudly on the pair, because heights here are tunable and a tune that inverts a line is otherwise completely silent.
_comment_aggressive: `aggressive` decides whether a wild pal will start a fight on its own. GAME_DESIGN.md 14 forbids simple proximity starting a fight with a PEACEFUL pal, and the same list allows 'Aggressive pal initiates' — so this flag is the line between those two rules, and it lives in data because it is a property of the creature, not of the code.

placeholder._comment_footprint: How long this body may be for its width, as a multiple of its collider diameter. A quadruped is genuinely several times longer than it is wide; a frog is not. Set too low and pal_body._fit() scales the model DOWN to fit the allowance and the creature renders shorter than its own collider claims — silently, until MA4.
placeholder._comment_art: Rigged and animated. The model is measured and fitted to `height` at load by pal_body._fit(), so the collider — and therefore the hit cone and the catch accuracy bonus — does not move when the art is swapped. `colour` is retained only for the fallback capsule.
placeholder._comment_animations: 26 clips ship baked into each .glb, so nothing is retargeted and nothing can be mangled. `pain` and `fall_over` are what hit and faint have wanted since M2; `uppercut` is a real committed swing rather than a lunge with no animation.
placeholder._comment_size: Chibi bipeds beside a 1.8m trainer, so they read as companions rather than as livestock — which is the Palworld register. Sized against each other so the practice creature is smaller than your partner and the one that ambushes you is bigger than both.
placeholder._comment_pack: Plumberry Plains Vol. 2, and it answers the review's first and largest complaint directly. The critic's words were 'none of them is a designed creature... Palworld's entire proposition is that its creatures are drawn characters — bold silhouette, hue-opposed to the environment, exaggerated proportion, expression', and that the previous roster put 'a naturalistic tree frog, a faceted grey low-poly goat, and a Nintendo Mii in the same 300 pixels'. These are ten designed chibi characters from ONE artist, which fixes the design AND the cohesion complaint at once.
placeholder._comment_pick:
Chosen on MEASURED colour, not taste. The first pick was fox, rabbit and wolf — which turned out to be the three LEAST saturated characters in the pack (0.20, 0.19, 0.15), i.e. exactly the defect the critic named on the creature they replaced: 'saturation 0.12... a grey rock standing on olive ground... your own pal is the least readable object in your own fight'. Re-picked against its stated criterion — hue-opposed to a green world, and readable at 40px:
  bear      hue  23 deg, sat 0.77, val 0.61  — orange-brown, the most saturated thing in the pack
  duck      hue  42 deg, sat 0.67, val 0.95  — bright gold
  songbird  hue 194 deg, sat 0.36, val 0.72  — blue, the only cool hue available
Three hues, three values, none of them the chartreuse the ground is made of.
placeholder._comment_role: Your partner, and therefore the one that must never be lost in a frame — so it gets the most saturated character in the pack.

ripplet._comment: Water starter. GAME_DESIGN.md 26: Water = balanced/efficient, so its statline sits between Terrapup's tank spread and the Air starter's offence.

placeholder._comment_footprint: Upright sitter with a torso-sized tail fan behind it; the fan is most of the footprint.
placeholder._comment_art: Produced by the tools/art_pipeline chain from sheet 02; see docs/art/RIPPLET_PRODUCTION_REPORT.md.

galewisp._comment: Air starter. GAME_DESIGN.md 26: Air = aggressive/fast-energy, so the highest attack and the thinnest armour of the three starters.

placeholder._comment_footprint: Spread wings make it far wider than deep; the allowance is for span, not body.
placeholder._comment_art: Produced by the tools/art_pipeline chain from sheet 03; see docs/art/production/.

bramblebun._comment: The practice creature. Peaceful, common, and generous to catch: it is the one the owner will throw at twenty times while deciding whether throwing is fun, and a rare target would make that a test of patience instead.

placeholder._comment_art: Produced by tools/art_pipeline from the owner's wild Ground Sheet A; see docs/art/MEADOWS_WILD_PRODUCTION_REPORT.md. Replaces the Plumberry duck that stood in for it. The model is measured and fitted to `height` at load by pal_body._fit(), so the collider — and therefore the hit cone and the catch accuracy bonus — does not move when the art is swapped. `colour` is retained only for the fallback capsule.

mudsnout._comment: The pre-evolution, and the only one in the biome (D13). A rooting runt: it is meant to read as young and unthreatening beside the thing it becomes, so it is the softest Ground creature in the roster and the second-easiest to catch after the practice rabbit.
mudsnout._comment_evolution: Recorded so the link survives in data. There is still no evolution SYSTEM in the project; this and tuskroot's `evolves_from` are the two ends of a rope nothing pulls on yet.

placeholder._comment_footprint: A low piglet is much longer than it is tall.

trailpup._comment: Tracker and flanker. The sheet's strengths are Speed, Tracking, Loyalty, so it is the roster's glass canine: it hits harder than anything else at its size and takes hits worse. Explicitly NOT the Ground starter -- no stone plates anywhere on it, which the canon pack names as a hard distinction.

placeholder._comment_footprint: Long-bodied and narrow -- the leanest silhouette in the Ground group.

tuskroot._comment: The one that comes at you. Tougher and rarer than the Hopper, because being ambushed should be a moment rather than an interruption — and because the first thing anyone does when something charges them is find out whether they can beat it.
tuskroot._comment_evolution: Tuskroot is no longer a base creature you meet in the wild — the owner's Meadows Wild Canon Pack makes it the evolved form of Mudsnout, and the ONLY evolution in the biome (docs/decisions/D13). Recorded here so the link is not lost. `mudsnout` now exists in this table, so both ends of the link are real; there is still no evolution SYSTEM in the project. The pair's heights are held apart by D17 and tests/test_evolution_links.gd: the evolved form must always be the larger one.

placeholder._comment_colour: Drawn from Tuskroot's own COLOR PALETTE row on docs/art/reference/wild/05_Meadows_Wild_Scale_Palette_Implementation_Guide.png (which despite its filename is Ground Sheet B) — the secondary fur/hide brown, which is what most of the body reads as in the turnarounds. Retained only for the fallback capsule, which is now genuinely a fallback: R0.6 installed a real rigged, animated, graded model.
placeholder._comment_art: R0.6: tools/art_pipeline finish.py clean -> texture -> rig -> grade -> install, from the R0.4 winner (candidate a). See docs/art/MEADOWS_WILD_PRODUCTION_REPORT.md. The model is measured and fitted to `height` at load by pal_body._fit(), so the collider — and therefore the hit cone and the catch accuracy bonus — does not move when the art is swapped. `colour` is retained only for the fallback capsule.

veridian._comment_type: Board 06 labels it Grass/Earth. The Meadows has three types — Ground, Water, Air — and REFERENCE_CANON's precedence rule is that the markdown wins on type while the image wins on looks, so it is the GROUND legendary per GAME_DESIGN.md section 26.
veridian._comment_catch: The lowest in the game by a wide margin. A legendary you catch on the second orb is not a legendary. TUNABLE.

placeholder._comment_size: Above every other creature in the biome, which D12 asked for explicitly: the range recentres at 1.35m for the practice creature and 2.00m for the ambusher, 'and the legendary above all of them'. At 2.6m it stands a head and antlers over the 1.8m trainer.
placeholder._comment_art: Board 06's Veridian Stag, owner-approved as the legendary's direct source. Antler rack thickened and bent forward per the blind critique — the generated rack swept backward only, 'which turns a crown into a windblown crest'.

_comment_wild_roster: The Meadows wild roster is canonised by docs/art/wild/ — twelve species plus one evolution. Species appear in this file as each is produced, because smoke_art.gd requires every entry to name a model that exists. Still to come: meadowhart, burrowback, paddlenewt, mosshell, brooktail, reedwing, pipwing, duskhush, galecrest. Heights follow D13: D12's peer band, keeping the sheets' relative ordering.
